subject: Histograms next to one another with same x and y scale

messages.author: 6c837d6a7caf2cda
messages.subject: Histograms next to one another with same x and y scale
parts:
Hi everybody,

I am creating several histograms for several size classes. Is there an
easy way to plot histograms next to one another with ggplot2 on the
same graph with the same continuous x and y scale. It should look
something like the lower part of this graph without the quantile
regression fitting:
http://addictedtor.free.fr/graphiques/RGraphGallery.php?graph=109

Cheers,

Kenneth

messages.author: deb3c9be98a98104
messages.subject: Controlling whiskers on boxplots
parts:
Is there a way to control the whiskers on a boxplot in ggplot (or in R)? I'd like to set them to 95th percentile rather than 1.5 IQR. There is supposedly such a command in the rgr package, but I don't see any change for different values of "wend"?

Thanks,
Mark

the spacing of the histograms should be in proportion to the
proportions between their respective sizeclasses. I hope this is
understandable. Can this be done with ggplot2 ???

Cheers,

Kenneth

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Histograms next to one another with same x and y scale
parts:
This is what I have so far...

ggplot(data=sizeclass, aes(x=parameter))+geom_histogram()+facet_grid(.~sizeclass)+coord_flip()

I don't think the facets can be graphed across like in your example so I'm not sure you can go any further. 

Brandon

messages.subject: Re: Histograms next to one another with same x and y scale
parts:
It's possible, but you have to do all the calculate by hand. The main
complication is that the y-axis isn't mapped to one variable - but is
a linear combination of time and count. I think this sort of plot
very often makes sense, but it's not entirely clear to me how it
should fit into the grammar.

Hadley

This parameter is currently fixed in ggplot2 - mainly because I think
it easily confuses readers who probably expect a standard boxplot.

Hadley
